newsitem.title: UK: ICCO agrees to set-up a reserve fund.
newsitem.headline: ICCO agrees to set-up a reserve fund.

text.p: The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) has agreed to set-up a reserve fund to finance the Group's administrative budget after its Buffer Stock sales run-out in April 1998.
"We have accepted the proposal but details are to be agreed upon at the next meeting in December," Hagen Streichert, the German delegate and spokesman for consumers told Reuters.
Buffer stock sales make up about forty percent of ICCO revenues but are due to run-out in April 1988, prompting the funding deficit.
It costs 2.7 million sterling a year to run the ICCO.

Another idea behind the reserve fund was that it could also serve as a liquidation fund, cushioning the blow should the ICCO ever be wound-up. Both consumers and producers have yet to narrow their differences over the size of the fund and when it will be implemented
Consumers have proposed a two million dollar fund against the Secetariat's idea of between 2.5 to 5.0 million dollars a year.
Producers are currently meeting to discuss the budget but they earlier proposed a three million dollar fund.
They said 40 percent of the fund shgould be raised from members contribution and 60 percent from Buffer Stock sales.
Other options being considered to help plug the shortfall include a substantial cut in the annual budget and a hefty increase in members contributions.
